subject: Food Science
title: Cold Chain Logistics
description: A fast breakdown of Cold Chain Logistics for builders.

hook.text: 40% of food in India spoils before reaching consumers—mostly because the cold chain is broken between farm and store.

buildup.text: The cold chain is an unbroken series of refrigerated transport and storage from harvest to consumer.

discovery.text: Every hour above 4°C doubles bacterial growth rates on fresh produce and meat. Gaps in the chain compound fast.

twist.text: Refrigerated shipping containers maintain 2°C across 6,000 miles of ocean—but the last mile to your kitchen is the weakest link.

climax.text: Smart sensors now track temperature continuously. If any link breaks the chain, the data reveals exactly where.

punchline.text: Cold from farm to fork. One broken link spoils everything downstream.

quiz.question: What happens when the cold chain is broken?
options: Bacterial growth rates double for every hour above safe temperatures
